advances: Exactly four consecutive integer fibers and common centrally symmetric middle body; endpoint shapes and anchors may differ.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
All continuous coordinates of the lifted hull lie in $B$; its two middle levels contain a full copy of $B$ and its two extreme base planes expose the prescribed endpoints. Thus the four fibers are exact. Test a non-pure-base closed cap through $(0,0)$ written $u\cdot x\ge tz$, $u\ne0$. The own middle copy contributes $b/2$. If $t\ge0$, the missed part of $A$ is contained in $B\cap\{u\cdot x<-t\}$, whose volume equals the captured volume of the other middle copy at threshold $t$ by central symmetry and the null boundary. Those two traces contribute at least $a$. If $t<0$, the missed part of $D$ is in $B\cap\{u\cdot x<2t\}$ of volume at most $b/2$, while the other middle trace at $t$ has volume at least $b/2$. Those two traces again contribute at least $a$. A pure-base cap through the mark contains its own middle copy and at least one whole endpoint. A containing cap includes its parallel through-mark cap, so the depth is at least $b/2+a$. Base reversal $z\mapsto1-z$ interchanges the two middle levels and the endpoints and gives the same lower bound at $(1,0)$.

For any nonzero $u$, take $L>\max_{x\in B}|u\cdot x|$. Each cap $\{\pm u\cdot x-Lz\ge0\}$ has mass $a+b/2$ because it contains $A$, halves the base-$0$ copy, and misses both positive base levels. Their union contains every continuous point over $z\le0$ because the sum of margins is $-2Lz$. Each cap $\{\pm u\cdot x+L(z-1)\ge0\}$ has the same mass, contains $D$, halves the base-$1$ copy, and misses the other two fibers. Their margins sum to $2L(z-1)$, so they cover all $z\ge1$. The four caps cover all integer bases and give the exact upper bound.

For independent contractions about $c_A\in A,c_D\in D$, convexity keeps both contracted endpoints in $B$; their equal volume is $a_t=(1-t)^da$. The preceding proof includes $a_t=0$, because the outer measures then vanish. The normalized expression is $(b/2+a_t)/(2(b+a_t))$, whose derivative with respect to $a_t$ is $b/[4(b+a_t)^2]>0$. At $t=1$ a pure-base cap isolates either singleton, proving its zero raw depth, while the normalized maximum is $1/4$.

statement: Let $d\ge1$, $B=-B$ be a convex body of $d$-volume $b>0$, and $A,D\subseteq B$ be convex bodies of the same $d$-volume $a$. The lifted convex hull of $A,B,B,D$ at bases $-1,0,1,2$ has exactly those four integer fibers. The maximum raw mixed closed-halfspace depth is $b/2+a$, attained at both $(0,0)$ and $(1,0)$. The same formula holds with singleton endpoints and $a=0$.
title: Exact depth with two centrally symmetric middle fibers and arbitrary equal-volume endpoints
